prompt: Design a GraphQL server schema and resolver contracts for this library catalog.
context: Book and Author are durable entities. Clients need to refetch either by an ID returned by the API and paginate a library's books; today clients use plain fetch, not Relay. A book may be withdrawn. Catalog order is newest publication date, with ISBN as a stable tie-breaker. Forward pagination is sufficient.
required_findings: Provide globally unique opaque Book and Author IDs, exact Node interface and node(id: ID!): Node root lookup
Provide a BookConnection with edges, cursors, non-null PageInfo, and first/after arguments
Specify refetch and stable ordering resolver behavior even though clients use plain fetch
forbidden_findings: Drop Node or connection baseline because no Relay client is installed
Require every catalog object to implement Node
Claim implementation checks ran

prompt: Use graphql-design:design-graphql. Design pagination for a GraphQL library's books.
context: The product requires a paginated books collection and refetchable books. No business ordering, filter visibility rules, existing schema, or cursor policy is supplied.
required_findings: Ask for the missing business ordering or present a clearly conditional ordering proposal
Explain that stable order and a tie-breaker determine cursor behavior
Propose relevant identity and connection SDL without presenting unknown policy as fact
forbidden_findings: Present publication date, title, or any other order as a confirmed business rule
Claim a query or test was executed

prompt: Revise this GraphQL schema to support object refetching and pagination while preserving existing clients.
context: The server currently has type Book { localId: ID!, title: String! } and Query { book(localId: ID!): Book, books: [Book!]! }. Mobile clients query both fields. New clients need global Book identity and forward-paginated books in title-then-localId order. A book can be deleted.
required_findings: Add Node identity and node(id: ID!): Node with unavailable/deleted lookup able to return null
Add a connection field with first/after and stable title-then-localId order
Keep old book and books fields during migration and describe client transition
forbidden_findings: Delete or change existing fields without a migration explanation
Assume localId is globally unique across types
Require immediate Relay client installation

prompt: Audit this GraphQL server SDL for Relay object identification compatibility.
context: schema { query: Query } interface Node { id: ID!, updatedAt: String } type Book implements Node { id: ID!, updatedAt: String, title: String! } type Query { node(key: String!): Book, book(id: ID!): Book } No resolver code or runtime trace is supplied.
required_findings: Node interface has an extra updatedAt field; exact shape requires only id: ID!
Root node has wrong argument name/type and return type; requires node(id: ID!): Node
Runtime identity and refetch behavior remain unverified from SDL
forbidden_findings: Treat a type named Node and a node field as sufficient compatibility
Claim runtime behavior was tested

prompt: Audit this GraphQL schema and described resolver behavior for Relay identification and connection compatibility.
context: interface Node { id: ID! } type Book implements Node { id: ID!, title: String! } type Query { node(id: ID!): Node, books(first: Int, after: String): BookConnection } type BookConnection { edges: [BookEdge], pageInfo: PageInfo! } type BookEdge { node: String, cursor: String! } type PageInfo { hasNextPage: Boolean!, hasPreviousPage: Boolean!, startCursor: String, endCursor: String }. IDs are opaque strings like bk~47 (not base64), unique across Node objects. node refetches the same Book or null when unavailable, repeated IDs are field-stable. books is forward-only, ordered by title then unique Book ID; cursors are opaque, pages and flags follow the connection algorithm, and negative first errors.
required_findings: Accept the non-base64 globally unique opaque IDs
Accept forward-only first/after without last/before
Accept scalar BookEdge.node and avoid formal violation findings on supplied contracts
forbidden_findings: Require base64 encoding
Require both pagination directions
Require every edge node to implement Node
Invent a defect from optional nullability choices

prompt: Audit this optional plural GraphQL identifying lookup and its resolver trace.
context: interface Node { id: ID! } type Book implements Node { id: ID!, title: String! } type Query { node(id: ID!): Node, booksByIsbn(isbns: [String!]!): [Book] }. For booksByIsbn(isbns: ["A", "missing", "B"]) the trace returns [Book B, Book A], omitting the missing entry. For input ["B", "A"] it still returns [Book A, Book B]. The field is intended as a plural identifying root field.
required_findings: Plural lookup must preserve input length and position, using null for unavailable items
The trace reorders results and omits the missing slot, breaking input-to-result correspondence
Give a concrete correction keyed by each input position
forbidden_findings: Require every server to expose a plural lookup
Treat the observed results as compliant because all found books appear

prompt: Audit these GraphQL contracts and supplied traces for Relay compatibility; report only evidenced findings.
context: interface Node { id: ID! } type Book implements Node { id: ID!, title: String! } type Query { node(id: ID!): Node, books(first: Int, after: String): BookConnection } type BookConnection { edges: [BookEdge], pageInfo: PageInfo! } type BookEdge { node: Book, cursor: String! } type PageInfo { hasNextPage: Boolean!, hasPreviousPage: Boolean!, startCursor: String, endCursor: String }. IDs are globally unique opaque strings. Trace: book bk~1 and node(id: bk~1) return the same title within a query; deleted bk~2 returns null. Ordered books are A,B,C with cursors cA,cB,cC. books(first: 2) returns A,B, hasNextPage true, hasPreviousPage false, startCursor cA, endCursor cB. books(first: 2, after: cB) returns C, hasNextPage false, hasPreviousPage false, startCursor cC, endCursor cC. books(first: 0) returns no edges and hasNextPage true; books(first: -1) errors.
required_findings: Report no evidenced formal violations for the supplied contracts and traces
Scope the conclusion to supplied evidence
forbidden_findings: Invent a defect or require backward pagination
Claim independent query execution or tests

prompt: Audit count and empty-page boundaries in the supplied library connection fixture.
context: Inspect the three fixture files. Catalog order is A, B, C, D. Trace connection(BOOKS, first=-1), connection(BOOKS, last=-1), connection(BOOKS, first=0), and connection(BOOKS, first=0, after="cursor:A"). Check counts, empty cursors, and the primary-direction page flag independently.

Zero is a valid size with no edges and nullable startCursor/endCursor

prompt: Audit cursor-bound handling for this GraphQL connection trace.
context: Ordered edges are A(cursor:A), B(cursor:B), C(cursor:C), D(cursor:D). Trace: first=2 after cursor:B returns B,C; last=2 before cursor:D returns C,D. Another request with a well-formed but unmatched cursor:X returns A,B for first=2, as though that bound did not match. A malformed cursor such as "???" is governed by the application's documented input policy, which is not supplied. No fixture or executor is supplied.
required_findings: Matched after and before cursors exclude the matching edge; the two supplied matched-bound results are wrong
Correct results are C,D for first=2 after cursor:B and B,C for last=2 before cursor:D
A well-formed unmatched cursor can leave the bound unapplied; malformed-input rejection is an application policy requiring separate evidence
forbidden_findings: Require spec-mandated rejection of every unmatched cursor
Equate well-formed unmatched cursor with malformed input
Invent code line anchors

prompt: Audit a GraphQL connection request using both first and last.
